key_insight: OPSD-V teaches few-step autoregressive video models from real long-video context so they can stay stable over long rollouts without changing their fast inference path. In simple terms, it reduces drift and motion collapse while keeping generation low-latency.
problem_solved: Few-step AR video generators are fast, but they often accumulate errors over time and lose realistic motion during long autoregressive generation. This paper addresses long-horizon degradation in post-trained video diffusion/generation models.
method: Use on-policy self-distillation to train the model on its own rollout behavior rather than only short, fixed training segments.
Inject real long-video data as temporal context during training to better match long-range dependencies.
Preserve the original few-step inference path, so the method improves quality without increasing generation latency.
impact: This matters for practitioners building fast video generation systems because it improves long-video consistency without sacrificing speed. It is especially useful for applications that need stable, coherent motion over extended sequences.
